known_limitations: The headline ratio is the work-normalized TFLOPS ratio (~1e-5 / ~87,000x). This is the architect-prescribed FAIR metric, but it stacks TWO deficits: (1) AXIOM computes 1/4096th of llama.cpp's output rows per dispatch, and (2) that single dispatch is dispatch-latency-dominated (316 us for 14336 MACs). Both are disclosed in ab_results.json (dims.note, fairness_caveat) and the prose. A reader must read the row-count caveat to interpret the 87,000x correctly — it is NOT '87,000x slower per equal work end-to-end'; it is the throughput gap of the FROZEN single-row kernel, which is the honest baseline M3.4 set out to quantify.
AMD/Intel halves not run (no cross-vendor hardware, EB.1) — deferred-not-dropped.
SPIRV-Headers had to be vendored locally to build llama.cpp Vulkan on this box (no root for apt). The script documents + automates this; a box with libvulkan-dev's full SDK would not need it.
deviations: Architect mentioned reporting a SECOND AXIOM row for full host-round-trip; the bench reports kernel-only GpuTimestamp MIN/MEAN/MEDIAN + sustained CPU-wall (which IS the host-inclusive per-dispatch number, since each dispatch_resident fence-waits). The sustained CPU-wall row covers the host-inclusive framing; a separate upload+readback-inclusive number was not added as it would not change the FAIL verdict and the spec's primary contract (kernel-only-vs-kernel-only) is satisfied.

Headline ratio uses TFLOPS (work-normalized) rather than raw us, because the n==1 case computes m=4096 rows on the llama.cpp side — a raw us ratio would be apples-to-oranges in AXIOM's favour. This matches the architect's 'TFLOPS is the fair metric' guidance and is labeled.
